city_served.value: Lady's Island, SC is served — one of the 12 towns claimed on the site, all confirmed by Paul 2026-10-06.
city_served.source: Brand Guide E (all 12 towns confirmed, Paul 2026-10-06); decisions-settled 'business' (12 towns)

local_context.value: Predominantly residential Sea Island in Beaufort County; elevation 16 ft; maritime upland forest, estuarine tidal and freshwater wetland ecosystems; since the late 20th century former plantation and timber tracts have been converted to residential subdivisions, so much of the housing is recent. Small portions are within the City of Beaufort; the majority is unincorporated. Climate/hurricane not stated on the page.

neighborhoods.value: 12 named in a Beaufort County Planning Commission staff report (CDPA-000015-2021, 2021-12-06; 'including, but not limited to'; county zoning district, some may since be annexed): Burckmeyer Beach, Captain Blythewood Landings, Tradewinds Plantation, Celadon, Brindlewood, Academy Estates, Magnolia Court, Deer Run, Royal Pines, Telfair, Christine Place, Spanish Moss. Not neighborhoods of Lady's Island: Cat Island, Distant Island (ambiguous), Dataw Island (own island, 'nearby islands' only, Paul 2026-10-12), Coosaw Point (historic site).

things_to_do.value: Whitehall Park (9.72 acres of pine and live oak on a salt-marsh point on the Beaufort River, 120 White Hall Drive; owned by Beaufort County, maintained by the City of Beaufort); Crystal Lake Park (Beaufort County Land Preservation park, 124 Lady's Island Drive); White Hall Boat Landing (county public boat landing, 33 Sea Island Parkway). No hours.

top_sites.value: Richard V. Woods Memorial Bridge (swing bridge between downtown Beaufort and Lady's Island, opened 1959, NRHP-listed 2023 — not the county table's 1988); Beaufort Executive Airport (general aviation, about 110 acres, 39 Airport Circle; also called Beaufort County Airport); Coosaw Point (historic site on the island's northeastern point).
